Package easyIO.regexp

package easyIO.regexp
Regular expressions with captures, matched using Brzozowski derivatives. The main classes to know about are:
  • Parser: parses the textual syntax of regular expressions, which is documented there. In brief: R|S, RS, R*, (R) for grouping, {R} for a capture, character classes [...], . for any character except a line break, and backslash escapes.
  • Matcher: matches a regular expression against a whole string or scanner input (match), the longest prefix at the current position (matchPrefix), or the first occurrence (search).
  • Match: one way the expression matched, giving the text captured by each capture group.
  • RegExp and its subclasses: regular expressions, which can also be built directly with factory methods such as Concat.concat, AlternationRE.alt, StarRE.star, and Capture.capture.
The convenience methods next, hasNext, and nextMatches of easyIO.Scanner use this package to scan input matching a pattern.

Matching never backtracks: it takes time linear in the length of the input, and constant stack space. Rather than choosing one match, a matcher reports all the ways the expression matches, each with its own captures. A capture may not occur inside a Kleene star.

Regular expressions are interned, and their derivatives are computed lazily and cached, forming a state machine that is shared by all matchers. These caches are safe to use from multiple threads, and a Matcher may be shared by several threads. They are never discarded, so a program that constructs many distinct regular expressions uses memory that grows accordingly.

Andrew Myers
